Entity morphing and grouping therefore come from the kit.","evidence":["Talk.tsx returns `&lt;Presentation className=&quot;htmp&quot; steps={STEPS} title=... initialMode=&quot;browse&quot; /&gt;`, imported from &#39;../../presentation-kit&#39;.","steps/index.ts maps OUTLINE through `defineStep({ ...beat, Scene: SampleScene, groupKey: &#39;scene&#39;, payload: { stage: index + 1 } })`.","steps/scene.tsx: `SampleScene({ payload }: SceneProps&lt;SamplePayload&gt;)` renders kit `SceneLayer`, `Presence` and `Appear`.","steps/layout.tsx and steps/parts.tsx build entities from kit `Box`, `Label`, `Arrow`, `Emphasis`, `Frame` and `SymbolChip`.","The nodes (`Box`, `Label`, `Frame`, `Emphasis`, `SymbolChip`) delegate to the kit&#39;s `EntityNode` (`motion.div` with `layout` and `layoutId={id}`). Every member of the grouped selectors is also prefixed. (2) The presentation template&#39;s style.css and (3) the bootstrap starter&#39;s style.css each hold only one rule, `.__SLUG__-box` and `.starter-box`. They contain no kit-hook selectors, element selectors or global rules; the hook examples sit inside a comment and are scoped under `.__SLUG__` / `.starter`. The class in each rule carries the presentation&#39;s own slug as a namespace, and only that presentation&#39;s own scene.tsx applies it. So the class works as that presentation&#39;s own hook and cannot match another presentation&#39;s elements after client-side navigation, which meets the criterion&#39;s &#39;own root class or hook&#39; clause and its stated concern. Judge C failed the criterion because `.starter-box` / `.__SLUG__-box` is not nested under `.starter` / `.__SLUG__`. That reason does not decide the requirement. The rules are not unscoped: each class is unique to its presentation and only that presentation&#39;s scene renders it. For a non-empty scratch workspace monorepo containing a working build anchor, `detect` selected `presentations/`, reported only kit/index missing, and required confirmation. The apply without `--confirmed` path was inspected in the initial probe; the confirmed run copied kit/index, skipped existing tooling and Landing files, kept the original `vite.config.ts` byte-equal to its seed and retained the root README, then built successfully. A subsequent bootstrap reported all anchors present and copied nothing. The starter/generated presentation and all required package dependencies were present. Source/template lookup worked through the absolute skill script path."},{"line":1257,"text":"3. **Creation, registry, routes, and coexistence (AT-001/AT-002): exercised in scratch.** The public scaffold command created a presentation folder and registry entry in an already scaffolded app. A second addition preserved the reference sample and first addition; the complete three-entry app built. `chrome-devtools-axi` opened `/how-to-make-a-presentation`, `/acceptance-generated`, and `/acceptance-third`; each route rendered its title/first step. The generated CSS remained inside the presentation folder, while kit source was not edited. Target-ambiguous modify and scoped-modify conversations were read in the skill contract only, not enacted; limitation above."},{"line":1258,"text":"4. **Whole app/reference sample and browser render (presentation-verification): exercised.** `npm run build` succeeded in an isolated scratch checkout. AXI opened the production sample at `http://127.0.0.1:5174/how-to-make-a-presentation`. Keyboard Right traversed indices 0 through 8 and showed all nine normative titles/captions in order. No AXI browser-console messages were found. The sample registry, marker numbering, captions, step count 9, and `data-step-index` were observed. Preview URLs used IPv4 `127.0.0.1`."},{"line":1259,"text":"5. **Grouped persistence, morph, enter/exit (evolving-scene): exercised.** The sample’s entity IDs accumulated across its nine steps as specified. Because the canonical sample never removes entities, a separate, authored-only-in-scratch two-step scene tested this kit seam: an existing entity kept the same DOM node while its canvas x-position moved; the departing node remained briefly at reduced opacity and was removed after exit; the newcomer appeared after the movement delay. This demonstrated in-place continuity, entry timing, and exit behavior without changing tracked files."},{"line":1260,"text":"6. **Modes, direct navigation, touch, active semantics, boundaries (evolving-scene / AT-003): exercised.** At step 7, `P` switched browse to present and preserved index 6; present mode exposed the marker/title while hiding caption, ToC, and prev/next controls. Returning to browse restored them. The ToC “the gathering” jumped from step 7 to its first step (index 2). A progress item exposed `aria-current=\"step\"` and `data-presentation-active=\"true\"`; the active ToC entry exposed `aria-current=\"true\"` and its active hook. Right/Left keyboard navigation traversed the deck. With body focus, Left at index 0 stayed at 0 and Right at index 8 stayed at 8. With a progress/ToC button focused, Arrow keys did not also navigate. Synthetic touch swipes moved back/forward as expected, horizontal swipe at the last step stayed clamped, and a vertical gesture did not navigate."},{"line":1261,"text":"7. **Canvas fit, attribution, and visual composition (AT-003): exercised; finding recorded.** Default canvas computed as 880×380. At 390×844 it fit to 342×147.7 and document width remained 390px (no horizontal overflow). Default attribution text/link and its styling hook were present; the URL was `https://github.com/Codagent-AI/and-scene`; top-left kit branding was absent. Screenshots show clean wide composition and the responsive composition. At 390px, scene labels scale to about 5px and are hard to read; this is **F-001**. Durable screenshots and text equivalents are in `acceptance-screenshots/README.md` and the adjacent PNGs."},{"line":1262,"text":"8. **Project-local screenshot helper (verification / AT-004 diagnostic seam): exercised.** On the unmodified scratch app, `node scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs how-to-make-a-presentation --no-build --settle 1000 --viewport 1440x900 --out .inspection-acceptance` completed with nine captures and zero warnings. Its report recorded each observed index 0–8, 0 running animations for each capture, and 1000ms settle configuration. A controlled scratch-only CSS fault then placed captions over header text, made active progress visually identical to inactive progress, and reduced attribution styling. The helper emitted step-specific overlap, active-chrome, and attribution warnings (54 total across the nine steps). This verifies warning detection and clean-sample behavior; it did not exercise the agent repair conversation or the allow-overlap suppression path. Those remain limitations."},{"line":1263,"text":"9. **Style neutrality / stable hooks / typed host boundary:** inspected in the running markup and source, with the app and generated template builds as integration evidence. Coverage floor results"},{"line":1254,"text":""},{"line":1255,"text":"1. **Skill gathering and author control (presentation-skill): partial.** Read the public workflow in `skills/presentation/SKILL.md`: it asks one question at a time for topic, style, and step details; permits explicit partial-detail continuation; treats mockups as optional; confirms targets before writing in non-empty projects; and scopes modifications to the selected presentation. An actual skill conversation was not run: this environment supplies no independent skill actor or human responses, and self-answering would not establish that the skill asks correctly. This is a limitation for AT-001, AT-002, and AT-004; see also the limitations below."},{"line":1256,"text":"2. **Standalone and partial monorepo scaffolding (AT-001 / self-bootstrapping): exercised.** From an empty scratch directory, `scaffold.mjs detect` reported all three anchors missing and no confirmation required; `bootstrap --apply` materialized the complete scaffold. `npm run build` succeeded. For a non-empty scratch workspace monorepo containing a working build anchor, `detect` selected `presentations/`, reported only kit/index missing, and required confirmation. The apply without `--confirmed` path was inspected in the initial probe; the confirmed run copied kit/index, skipped existing tooling and Landing files, kept the original `vite.config.ts` byte-equal to its seed and retained the root README, then built successfully. A subsequent bootstrap reported all anchors present and copied nothing. The starter/generated presentation and all required package dependencies were present. Source/template lookup worked through the absolute skill script path."},{"line":1257,"text":"3. **Creation, registry, routes, and coexistence (AT-001/AT-002): exercised in scratch.** The public scaffold command created a presentation folder and registry entry in an already scaffolded app. A second addition preserved the reference sample and first addition; the complete three-entry app built. `chrome-devtools-axi` opened `/how-to-make-a-presentation`, `/acceptance-generated`, and `/acceptance-third`; each route rendered its title/first step. The generated CSS remained inside the presentation folder, while kit source was not edited. Target-ambiguous modify and scoped-modify conversations were read in the skill contract only, not enacted; limitation above."},{"line":1258,"text":"4. **Whole app/reference sample and browser render (presentation-verification): exercised.** `npm run build` succeeded in an isolated scratch checkout. AXI opened the production sample at `http://127.0.0.1:5174/how-to-make-a-presentation`. Keyboard Right traversed indices 0 through 8 and showed all nine normative titles/captions in order. No AXI browser-console messages were found. The sample registry, marker numbering, captions, step count 9, and `data-step-index` were observed. Preview URLs used IPv4 `127.0.0.1`."},{"line":1259,"text":"5. **Grouped persistence, morph, enter/exit (evolving-scene): exercised.** The sample’s entity IDs accumulated across its nine steps as specified. Because the canonical sample never removes entities, a separate, authored-only-in-scratch two-step scene tested this kit seam: an existing entity kept the same DOM node while its canvas x-position moved; the departing node remained briefly at reduced opacity and was removed after exit; the newcomer appeared after the movement delay. This demonstrated in-place continuity, entry timing, and exit behavior without changing tracked files."},{"line":1260,"text":"6. **Modes, direct navigation, touch, active semantics, boundaries (evolving-scene / AT-003): exercised.** At step 7, `P` switched browse to present and preserved index 6; present mode exposed the marker/title while hiding caption, ToC, and prev/next controls. Returning to browse restored them. The ToC “the gathering” jumped from step 7 to its first step (index 2). A progress item exposed `aria-current=\"step\"` and `data-presentation-active=\"true\"`; the active ToC entry exposed `aria-current=\"true\"` and its active hook. Right/Left keyboard navigation traversed the deck. With body focus, Left at index 0 stayed at 0 and Right at index 8 stayed at 8. With a progress/ToC button focused, Arrow keys did not also navigate. Synthetic touch swipes moved back/forward as expected, horizontal swipe at the last step stayed clamped, and a vertical gesture did not navigate."},{"line":1261,"text":"7. **Canvas fit, attribution, and visual composition (AT-003): exercised; finding recorded.** Default canvas computed as 880×380. At 390×844 it fit to 342×147.7 and document width remained 390px (no horizontal overflow). Default attribution text/link and its styling hook were present; the URL was `https://github.com/Codagent-AI/and-scene`; top-left kit branding was absent. Screenshots show clean wide composition and the responsive composition. At 390px, scene labels scale to about 5px and are hard to read; this is **F-001**. Durable screenshots and text equivalents are in `acceptance-screenshots/README.md` and the adjacent PNGs."},{"line":1262,"text":"8. **Project-local screenshot helper (verification / AT-004 diagnostic seam): exercised.** On the unmodified scratch app, `node scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs how-to-make-a-presentation --no-build --settle 1000 --viewport 1440x900 --out .inspection-acceptance` completed with nine captures and zero warnings. Its report recorded each observed index 0–8, 0 running animations for each capture, and 1000ms settle configuration. A controlled scratch-only CSS fault then placed captions over header text, made active progress visually identical to inactive progress, and reduced attribution styling. The helper emitted step-specific overlap, active-chrome, and attribution warnings (54 total across the nine steps). This verifies warning detection and clean-sample behavior; it did not exercise the agent repair conversation or the allow-overlap suppression path. Those remain limitations."},{"line":1263,"text":"9. **Style neutrality / stable hooks / typed host boundary:** inspected in the running markup and source, with the app and generated template builds as integration evidence. The scene exposes stable entity hooks, chrome exposes active/current semantics, and a typed grouped-payload scene compiled at the presentation boundary. Kit primitives add behavior/hooks and geometry; sample look is in presentation CSS. No Tailwind dependency or kit-owned visual palette was found. Default attribution is present; host brand remains opt-in."}],"label":"[artifact candidate-65e455a7e181efb2 (exploration-log)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":1265,"end_line":1270,"lines":[{"line":1265,"text":"## Exploration beyond the floor"},{"line":1266,"text":""},{"line":1267,"text":"1. **Scaffold/process seam — no defect found.** Prediction: target selection would be root for an empty standalone and `presentations/` for the monorepo; a missing-anchor apply would require confirmation and preserve preexisting files. The first disposable setup was invalid (see failed probes); it is recorded separately rather than attributed to the product."},{"line":1268,"text":"2. **Registry/generated-route seam — no defect found.** Prediction: adding presentations would append registry entries, leave prior route folders reachable, and build all registered routes. Observation: three entries built and all three routes opened in AXI at their first steps."},{"line":1269,"text":"3. **Grouped browser-state seam — no defect found.** Prediction: grouped scene transitions would retain DOM identity for a continuing node, move it, delay newcomer opacity, and remove a departing node after its exit. dispute_checks{"demo-integration":[],"scene-kit":[],"presentation-skill":[],"verification-tooling":[],"engineering-quality":[{"id":"engineering-preview-terminated-on-every-exit","classification":"contradicted","rationale":"The auditor&#39;s observation is accurate but does not defeat the pass. On every exit path the guidance names (success, failing check, browser launch failure, error after the preview started), all four entry scripts reach `await stopAll()` in an outer finally. stopAll sends SIGTERM to the detached Vite process group: the server itself, spawned via process.execPath, not an npm or npx wrapper. It then polls until exitCode or signalCode is set, so the exit is awaited. The SIGKILL branch without a further await runs only if Vite ignores SIGTERM for 3 seconds. That is a hypothetical the guidance does not name and the evidence does not show. Even in that case SIGKILL, which cannot be ignored, goes to the server&#39;s own process group, so the server does not keep running. None of the guidance&#39;s fail conditions applies: a wrapper-only kill, a preview left running after a launch failure or later error, or a copy lacking cleanup.","evidence":["scripts/lib/runtime.mjs startPreview spawns `process.execPath [vite.js, &#39;preview&#39;, ...]` with `detached: true` and adds it to `children`.","stopAll(): `killGroup(child, &#39;SIGTERM&#39;)`, then `while (running.some(child =&gt; child.exitCode === null &amp;&amp; child.signalCode === null)) { ... await sleep(50) }`, so exit is awaited on …","scripts/verify.mjs main(): try { build; registration; renderSample } catch {...} finally { await stopAll() }. chromium.launch() runs inside renderSample, so a launch failure reaches the finally.","scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs top level: try { await main() } catch {...} finally { await stopAll() }. chromium.launch() runs inside main after startPreview.","The bootstrap template copies are identical, and tests/integration/bootstrap.test.ts asserts byte parity for verify.mjs, inspect-presentation.mjs and lib/runtime.mjs.","tests/integration/verify.test.ts and inspect.test.ts assert listProcesses(`.../vite.js preview`) is empty after success, browser launch failure, a mid-run browser crash and SIGTERM interruption."],"citations":["scripts/lib/runtime.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/lib/runtime.mjs","scripts/verify.mjs","scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/verify.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs","tests/integration/bootstrap.test.ts","tests/integration/verify.test.ts","tests/integration/inspect.test.ts"],"marker":"","stage":"contradiction-check","panel_index":2,"sample":3},{"id":"engineering-preview-readiness-bounded","classification":"contradicted","rationale":"The readiness wait in both copies of runtime.mjs does have a timeout: startPreview sets a 30-second deadline and throws `preview server not ready` once it passes. The other readiness waits are bounded too. The loop that waits for the printed URL stops after 20 tries, and both verify and inspect pass STEP_TIMEOUT_MS to waitForSelector and waitForFunction. The auditor&#39;s case needs the server on 127.0.0.1 to accept the probe connection and then never answer it. The material does not show that happening. It is a made-up input, and the review guidance does not name it: the guidance fails a readiness wait only when it &#39;has no timeout&#39;, and this one has one. When nothing is listening yet, fetch is refused right away, the catch block runs, and the loop goes back to the deadline check. Leaving out a per-request AbortSignal does not mean the readiness wait has no timeout. The other two clauses are met: both scripts await the build before calling startPreview, and the printed URL is collected across chunks and has its ANSI codes stripped.","evidence":["scripts/lib/runtime.mjs startPreview: `const deadline = Date.now() + 30_000` and, on each pass, `if (Date.now() &gt; deadline) throw new Error(`preview server not ready at ${probeUrl}`)` before `awai…","The printed-URL wait is bounded: `for (let wait = 0; wait &lt; 20 &amp;&amp; !urlPattern.test(stripAnsi(output)); wait++) await sleep(100)`. Output is collected with `output += chunk` and has its ANS…","scripts/verify.mjs main awaits build() before renderSample() calls startPreview(). scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs awaits runNpm(&#39;build&#39;) before startPreview().","Page readiness waits use `{ timeout: STEP_TIMEOUT_MS }` in both verify and inspect.","The template copies under skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts match the repository copies.","Nothing in the material shows a probe that the preview server accepts but never answers. The guidance does not name this scenario, and the instructions say not to fail a criterion on a hypothetical i…"],"citations":["scripts/lib/runtime.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/lib/runtime.mjs","scripts/verify.mjs","scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/verify.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs"],"marker":"","stage":"contradiction-check","panel_index":2,"sample":3}],"testing-evidence":[],"assumption-handling":[]}
